articles.title: Novas regras para patinetes e bicicletas elétricas começam a valer nesta sexta em SP, mas fiscalização fica para outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Novas regras estabelecem limites de velocidade, regras de circulação e restrições para bicicletas elétricas, patinetes e outros veículos autopropelidos na capital.
articles.summary: Novas regras estabelecem limites de velocidade, regras de circulação e restrições para bicicletas elétricas, patinetes e outros veículos autopropelidos na capital.
articles.body:
Duas pessoas em um patinete elétrico em Paris — Foto: Sarah Meyssonnier/Reuters

As novas regras para a circulação de bicicletas elétricas, patinetes e outros equipamentos elétricos individuais começam a valer nesta sexta-feira (28) na cidade de São Paulo , mas a fiscalização só terá início em 12 de outubro, segundo decisão da prefeitura.

Segundo portaria da Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade e Trânsito (SMT), neste primeiro momento serão realizadas apenas campanhas educativas e ações de orientação aos usuários .

A regulamentação estabelece onde cada tipo de veículo pode circular e quais são os limites de velocidade. Entre as principais mudanças, patinetes elétricos ficam proibidos de circular em calçadas e áreas exclusivas para pedestres e só poderão trafegar em ruas e avenidas com velocidade máxima de 40 km/h.

Já as bicicletas elétricas poderão circular em ruas com limite de até 50 km/h quando não houver ciclovia ou ciclofaixa disponível. Nas ciclovias e ciclofaixas instaladas na pista, a velocidade máxima será de 20 km/h.

As regras foram publicadas pela Prefeitura de São Paulo em 14 de agosto e foram elaboradas em meio à expansão dos serviços de compartilhamento de patinetes na capital. Dados das duas empresas autorizadas a operar na cidade indicam que a frota conjunta passou de 2 mil para 7,1 mil equipamentos entre o fim de 2024 e agosto de 2025.

A regulamentação não se aplica aos ciclomotores, categoria que engloba veículos de duas ou três rodas com motor elétrico de até 4 kW ou motor a combustão de até 50 cilindradas e velocidade máxima de fabricação de 50 km/h. Esses veículos estão sujeitos às regras nacionais de trânsito, que incluem registro, emplacamento, capacete e habilitação.

Diferenças entre bicicleta elétrica, autopropelido e ciclomotor — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Patinetes elétricos e outros equipamentos conduzidos em pé

ciclovias, ciclofaixas e ciclorrotas: até 20 km/h;

ciclofaixas compartilhadas com pedestres: até 6 km/h;

ruas e avenidas: permitidos apenas em vias com limite de até 40 km/h, e o equipamento não pode passar de 20 km/h;

proibidos em calçadas e áreas exclusivas para pedestres;

proibidos em vias com velocidade regulamentada acima de 40 km/h.

ciclovias e ciclofaixas na pista: até 20 km/h;

espaços compartilhados com pedestres: até 6 km/h;

podem circular em ruas com limite de até 50 km/h quando não houver infraestrutura cicloviária;

nesses casos, devem seguir junto à margem da pista e no mesmo sentido dos demais veículos;

continuam proibidas em vias de trânsito rápido e rodovias sem acostamento ou faixa própria, ressalvadas as exceções previstas para bicicletas de uso esportivo.

As mesmas regras de circulação previstas para as bicicletas elétricas também valem para as bicicletas convencionais.

Pelas regras do Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (Contran), bicicleta elétrica é aquela equipada com motor auxiliar de até 1.000 watts, acionado somente enquanto o condutor pedala.

O veículo não pode ter acelerador, e a assistência do motor deve ser interrompida quando atingir 32 km/h.

A regulamentação também abrange os chamados equipamentos de mobilidade individual autopropelidos, categoria na qual estão patinetes, skates e monociclos elétricos.

Segundo o Contran, esses equipamentos podem ter motor de até 1.000 watts e velocidade máxima de fabricação de 32 km/h. Ao contrário das bicicletas elétricas, eles podem ter acelerador.

Há ainda os autopropelidos conduzidos sentados ou montados, como determinados modelos de scooters elétricas que, pelas características técnicas, não são classificados como ciclomotores.

Esses veículos poderão circular em ciclovias e ciclofaixas a até 20 km/h e, quando não houver infraestrutura cicloviária, em vias com velocidade regulamentada de até 50 km/h. Em áreas compartilhadas com pedestres, o limite é de 6 km/h.

A circulação é proibida em áreas destinadas exclusivamente a pedestres e em vias com limite acima de 50 km/h.

A regulamentação foi submetida a consulta pública pela Prefeitura de São Paulo entre maio e junho. Durante o período, moradores, especialistas e entidades puderam enviar sugestões pela plataforma Participe+.

A portaria municipal tem como base a Resolução 996 do Contran, que estabeleceu as regras nacionais para bicicletas elétricas, equipamentos autopropelidos e ciclomotores e atribuiu aos municípios a regulamentação da circulação desses veículos em suas vias.

articles.title: Como empreendedora transformou crochê em negócio de R$ 40 mil por mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Após enfrentar dificuldades financeiras, Teruko Kato transformou uma habilidade aprendida na infância em uma marca autoral de produtos para bebês, administrada ao lado das filhas.
articles.summary: Teruko Kato começou vendendo sapatinhos artesanais para bebês na rua e hoje divide a gestão da marca com as duas filhas.
articles.body:
Antes mesmo de dar os primeiros passos, alguns bebês já começam a vida com muito estilo. E, em São Paulo , uma empreendedora encontrou justamente nos pezinhos dos recém-nascidos a oportunidade de reconstruir a própria trajetória.

Aos 11 anos, Teruko Kato aprendeu a fazer crochê. Durante décadas, no entanto, a habilidade ficou guardada entre tantas outras experiências profissionais.

Ela trabalhou como manicure, esteticista, maquiadora e vendedora de bijuterias, sempre movida pelo desejo de ter o próprio negócio.

Mas foi em um dos momentos mais difíceis da vida que o crochê voltou a ocupar um papel central. "Eu só tinha dívidas, uma geladeira vazia e duas crianças que contavam comigo. Então eu comecei a fazer crochê de volta por terapia", conta.

O que começou como uma forma de aliviar a ansiedade se transformou em uma ideia de negócio. Logo, a casa estava cheia de sapatinhos artesanais para bebês . Faltava apenas encontrar compradores.

Sem recursos para abrir uma loja e receosa de montar uma barraca na rua, Teruko encontrou uma solução criativa: transformou uma bicicleta em ponto de venda itinerante.

Ela passou a circular pela Avenida Paulista oferecendo os produtos. A escolha não foi por acaso. "Eu tive a ideia de vender na Paulista porque achava que a rua era o melhor caminho para ganhar dinheiro rápido", lembra.

Com a documentação regularizada, ela passou anos vendendo os produtos diretamente ao público . Aos poucos, descobriu um nicho pouco explorado na região: presentes artesanais para bebês.

A estratégia funcionou. Da bicicleta, o negócio migrou para feiras voltadas ao setor de maternidade e começou a ganhar visibilidade.

Como empreendedora transformou crochê em negócio de R$ 40 mil por mês — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

Enquanto a mãe consolidava a produção artesanal, a filha Bárbara Naomi construía outra frente importante para a empresa.

Estudante de Publicidade à época, ela usou a própria marca da família como objeto de estudo na faculdade. Os trabalhos acadêmicos ajudaram a desenhar o planejamento de marketing que mais tarde seria colocado em prática .

Hoje, Bárbara lidera as áreas de comunicação, produção de conteúdo, fotografia, vídeo e redes sociais. Segundo ela, os vídeos se tornaram uma das principais portas de entrada para novos clientes.

"Os roteiros viralizam, estouram a bolha. É assim que a gente consegue chegar a pessoas que talvez nunca estivessem procurando especificamente um sapatinho de crochê", afirma.

A estratégia digital ampliou significativamente o alcance da marca e ajudou a transformar clientes ocasionais em consumidores recorrentes.

O principal diferencial da empresa está na originalidade das peças . Em vez de modelos tradicionais, Teruko desenvolveu uma coleção inspirada em animais. Hoje são cerca de 50 modelos diferentes , incluindo ouriço, lobo-guará, baleia, tigre, onça, rato e coelho.

O processo criativo é totalmente autoral. "Aqui é criação. Não tem cópia. Quando encontro um animal que acho fofinho, pego a linha e vou construindo", explica.

Cada par custa, em média, R$ 350 e é produzido manualmente com fio 100% algodão . O cuidado vai além da estética.

"Depois que termino, passo a mão para sentir se tem algum nozinho na linha. Um nó pode incomodar o bebê", diz a empreendedora.

A emoção também faz parte da proposta do produto. "Fui descobrindo esse outro lado do sapato, o lado do afeto."

Com a evolução das vendas, a família decidiu investir em um espaço próprio. A abertura da loja exigiu um investimento de R$ 25 mil e foi planejada estrategicamente na região da Paulista , área que Teruko conhece bem desde os tempos da bicicleta.

O conceito do espaço também reflete o DNA artesanal da marca. Além da vitrine, o local permite que os clientes acompanhem a produção dos produtos.

"Eu queria que as pessoas me vissem trabalhando para entender que aquilo é feito de verdade", afirma.

A loja se tornou um importante canal de vendas e contribuiu para aumentar o ticket médio dos consumidores, que muitas vezes levam conjuntos completos de presentes.

A proposta afetiva tem conquistado consumidores muito além das fronteiras brasileiras. A cliente Cínthia Avelar, por exemplo, encontrou a marca pela internet e comprou um par de sapatinhos em formato de ouriço para presentear a cunhada grávida, que mora na Alemanha.

"Meu irmão mora lá desde 2014 e foi ele quem me apresentou o ouriço. É um animal muito lindinho. Caiu como uma luva", conta.

Além dos sapatinhos, a empresa também comercializa naninhas, pelúcias e ponchos para bebês. Atualmente, o negócio registra um faturamento mensal de aproximadamente R$ 40 mil .

Hoje, Teruko divide a gestão da empresa com as filhas Bárbara e Laura Suemi, estudante de Direito que também já integra a operação.

A convivência intensa, dentro e fora do trabalho, é vista como um dos grandes trunfos da marca. "Eu acho ótimo. Está tudo debaixo da minha asa", brinca Teruko.

Apesar do crescimento, a família ainda vê espaço para avançar. O desafio imediato é ampliar a capacidade produtiva de um negócio baseado em trabalho manual . Mais adiante, o objetivo é cruzar fronteiras.

"Tem dois lugares que considero icônicos, assim como São Paulo: Paris e Nova York", diz a empreendedora.

Depois de transformar uma habilidade aprendida na infância em uma empresa familiar, Teruko acredita que o principal segredo continua sendo valorizar o próprio trabalho.

"Primeiro você dá valor ao que faz para que as pessoas valorizem também", conta a empreendedora.

E foi exatamente assim, ponto por ponto, que ela construiu um negócio capaz de transformar dificuldades em oportunidades e afeto em empreendedorismo.

articles.title: Mais data centers, mais energia: por que a expansão da IA abre disputa sobre a conta de luz | G1
articles.standfirst: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.summary: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.body:
A inteligência artificial depende de grandes centros de dados, que reúnem milhares de chips e consomem muita eletricidade. A Agência Internacional de Energia estima que o consumo dos data centers no mundo possa mais que dobrar até 2030.

O Brasil pode ganhar espaço nessa corrida por ter uma matriz elétrica com forte presença de fontes renováveis, como hidrelétrica, solar e eólica. Mas há um gargalo: nem toda a energia disponível consegue chegar a quem precisa dela.

Se a demanda dos data centers crescer mais rápido que a infraestrutura elétrica, será preciso investir para produzir mais energia e ampliar a rede que leva essa eletricidade até os consumidores.

A discussão é sobre quem vai pagar essa conta: as empresas responsáveis pelo aumento do consumo ou, dependendo de como os custos forem divididos, também os demais consumidores na conta de luz.

Toda semana, o g1 Explica simplifica a economia, o mercado financeiro e a educação financeira, mostrando como tudo isso afeta o seu bolso.

articles.title: RS terá mais 3 dias de chuva forte, granizo e rajadas de vento; veja | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria perde velocidade e favorece sequência de temporais em diversas regiões do estado. Volumes acumulados podem superar 200 mm em áreas dos Vales e da Serra.
articles.summary: Frente fria perde velocidade e favorece sequência de temporais em diversas regiões do estado. Volumes acumulados podem superar 200 mm em áreas dos Vales e da Serra.
articles.body:
O Rio Grande do Sul deve enfrentar uma sequência de temporais até o fim de semana, com previsão de chuva forte, granizo e rajadas de vento que podem superar 90 km/h .

Conforme a Climatempo Meteorologia, a frente fria responsável pela instabilidade avança lentamente sobre a região, o que favorece a repetição dos episódios de chuva e aumenta a preocupação com os volumes acumulados até o fim de semana .

Nesta sexta-feira (28), as áreas de instabilidade se espalham por todo o estado. Os acumulados previstos variam entre 10 e 80 milímetros ao longo do dia , mas podem ultrapassar 110 milímetros em pontos do Sul, da Campanha, da Costa Doce e do Litoral Norte. Parte dessa chuva pode ocorrer em curto intervalo de tempo.

Outro fator de atenção é o vento. Na metade Norte do estado, rajadas entre 60 e 80 km/h podem ser registradas mesmo fora das áreas de tempestade.

Segundo a Climatempo, a distribuição das áreas com maior risco muda ao longo do dia. Depois de um primeiro momento com preocupação concentrada no Sul do estado, a tendência é de que a instabilidade avance em direção ao Centro, à Região Metropolitana, aos Vales, à Serra e a áreas do Norte e do Nordeste gaúcho.

Na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre , a previsão indica continuidade do risco de temporais, granizo, chuva intensa e ventos fortes. A preocupação também está relacionada à sequência de episódios de precipitação, que pode elevar os acumulados ao longo de vários períodos de chuva . As temperaturas máximas não devem passar de 21°C na capital e arredores.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu avisos de tempestade válidos para esta sexta-feira, com graus de severidade classificados entre "perigo potencial" e "perigo". V eja mapa abaixo.

Previsão de tempestade para sexta-feira (28) no RS — Foto: Divulgação/ Inmet

No sábado (29), a frente fria deve permanecer praticamente estacionada sobre o Sul do Brasil , mantendo o transporte de umidade e a formação de novas áreas de instabilidade.

As regiões com maior risco passam a ser Missões, Centro-Norte, Noroeste, Norte, Nordeste, Serra, Vales, Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre e Litoral Norte.

Os volumes previstos ficam entre 10 e 70 milímetros, mas podem passar de 120 milímetros em pontos dos Vales, da Serra e do Litoral Norte.

De acordo com a Climatempo, a principal preocupação passa a ser o acumulado da sequência de dias chuvosos . Em áreas dos Vales e da Serra, o volume total de chuva pode superar 200 milímetros ao longo do período, cenário que exige atenção devido à resposta mais rápida das bacias hidrográficas dessas regiões.

Domingo ainda terá reflexos da instabilidade

Chuva no RS — Foto: Porthus Junior/Agência RBS

No domingo (30), a chuva tende a avançar mais para Santa Catarina e Paraná , mas o Rio Grande do Sul ainda sentirá os efeitos dos dias consecutivos de instabilidade .

A atenção deve permanecer voltada principalmente para as regiões do Centro ao Norte do estado, onde a chuva mais persistente está prevista.

Já na metade Sul, incluindo Oeste, Campanha e Sudeste, o tempo tende a ficar mais estável, sem previsão de episódios intensos.

articles.title: Convênio vai levar aula de empreendedorismo para as escolas | G1
articles.standfirst: Parceria entre a Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras e o Sebrae RJ vai beneficiar os alunos do Ensino Fundamental.
articles.summary: Parceria entre a Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras e o Sebrae RJ vai beneficiar os alunos do Ensino Fundamental.
articles.body:
O convênio vai permitir aulas de empreendedorismo na rede pública de ensino — Foto: Secom

Um convênio de cooperação técnica entre a Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras e o Sebrae, assinado no Gabinete da Sede Administrativa, vai permitir que a Secretaria Municipal de Educação, Esporte e Lazer inclua na grade curricular aulas de empreendedorismo, por meio do Plano de Trabalho de Educação Empreendedora Básica, com a implantação do curso “Jovens Empreendedores – 1os Passos nas Escolas”.

A princípio esse curso será implantado em 26 unidades escolares, beneficiando cerca de 7 mil alunos do 1º ao 9º ano do Ensino Fundamental. A iniciativa visa capacitar professores e desenvolver competências socioemocionais, cidadania e autonomia nos alunos da Educação Básica, alinhando-se às diretrizes da Base Nacional Comum Curricular. Dentre os objetivos também estão o desenvolvimento de competências, focando em atitudes, autoconhecimento e resolução de problemas. No lugar de apenas abrir empresas, o curso estimula o protagonismo, engajando os alunos na construção de seus projetos de vida e planos de metas.

Para o prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar, a ideia é investir cada vez mais na formação dos alunos da Rede Municipal para que a Educação continue sendo um destaque em Rio das Ostras. “Este é um projeto consolidado desenvolvido por uma instituição respeitável, que é o Sebrae. Por isso, estamos criando políticas públicas inovadoras na Educação, fazendo o desenvolvimento pleno nas escolas públicas. A ideia é fazer com que o conteúdo pedagógico seja acrescido de conhecimento sobre empreendedorismo para potencializar os alunos a conseguir êxito no competitivo mercado de trabalho”, declarou Carlos Augusto.

As analistas de negócios do Sebrae RJ Angélica Pagini e Camilla Souza ressaltaram que esse convênio é uma oportunidade de desenvolver habilidades empreendedoras nos alunos da Rede. “O Projeto Jovens Empreendedores do Sebrae busca trazer uma formação empreendedora para os alunos dentro de sala de aula. A ideia é que o curso traga o protagonismo para que esses estudantes sejam criativos e desenvolvam suas capacidades e habilidades de forma empreendedora, para que tenham um futuro próspero no mercado de trabalho”, analisou Angélica.

A secretária de Educação do Município, Marcele Raquel de Mattos Martins, destacou que a educação empreendedora, dentro do projeto pedagógico escolar, representa a formação do aluno na perspectiva integral de cada um como cidadão.

“É uma forma de fortalecer as habilidades desses jovens para que eles possam detectar oportunidades na sociedade, que é altamente competitiva. Essa inovação vai agregar conhecimento e preparação para a vida dos alunos. Os professores da nossa Rede serão orientados e receberão a preparação necessária para que eles possam passar o conteúdo para os alunos de forma simples e objetiva. Dessa forma, nossos estudantes já sairão com um encaminhamento melhor para o mercado de trabalho”, informou a secretária.

articles.title: El Rubius GTA 6 controversy explained as streamer hits back at "sellout" accusations over Rockstar collaboration
articles.summary: US Streamers News: El Rubius has found himself at the center of a GTA 6 debate after announcing an exclusive video created following his visit to Rockstar North. What lo.
articles.body: El Rubius has found himself at the center of a GTA 6 debate after announcing an exclusive video created following his visit to Rockstar North. What looked like exciting news for fans quickly turned into criticism, with some viewers accusing the Spanish streamer of being too friendly toward Rockstar. Rubius has now pushed back, denying that he was paid and reminding fans that he has criticized the developer before.El Rubius faces backlash over GTA 6 exclusive Rockstar contentThe controversy began after El Rubius revealed that his YouTube channel would soon feature exclusive GTA 6 content following a visit to Rockstar North in Edinburgh. The trip reportedly took place in July, when a small group of creators were given a private, hands-off look at the highly anticipated game.Rubius shared his excitement on X, describing the opportunity as a dream and thanking Rockstar Games for inviting him."I've visited Rockstar North. GTA VI. Tomorrow the secret comes to an end. You'll have on my channel an EXCLUSIVE video with unseen images and all the details of the BIGGEST game in history. This is a dream 😭. Thanks for inviting me to your home ❤️, @RockstarGames."The announcement did not land well with everyone. Some fans questioned whether his relationship with Rockstar had influenced his previous comments about the company's decisions, particularly its approach to GTA 6's physical release.One critic called him a "sellout," while others connected the collaboration to Rockstar's decision to distribute the boxed version of GTA 6 with a download code instead of traditional physical game media.El Rubius responds to GTA 6 "sellout" criticismRubius quickly addressed the accusations rather than allowing the criticism to build around his announcement. He said Rockstar had not paid him for the video and pointed out that copyrighted music would prevent him from earning money from it."To clarify: Rockstar hasn’t paid me for this. My video will have music with copyright, so I won’t earn anything from that either. I already criticized the physical format thing back then (I even made a dedicated video about it, but you probably didn’t see it because it didn’t go viral, and you’ll have let yourselves be swayed by 10-second clips like always). I criticized Rockstar back then when they released the remastered trilogy."The streamer also appeared frustrated by what he viewed as a distorted version of his past comments. He argued that criticism he had previously made was being overlooked because short clips were shaping the conversation.Rubius then took a stronger stance against the backlash, urging critics to focus their attention elsewhere."It’s because of stuff like this that I can no longer take the 'funas' seriously. You live in an altered reality where you create your own narratives and repeat them so much that you end up believing them. Let go of my arm and go find yourselves a real problem already, for God’s sake."The dispute comes as interest in GTA 6 reaches another major moment, with Rockstar's highly anticipated game continuing to dominate gaming discussions. For Rubius, however, the excitement surrounding his exclusive footage has been accompanied by an unexpected argument over trust, criticism and his relationship with Rockstar.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Will send Netanyahu to hell’: Iran warns of ‘confrontation’ if US blockade continues
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran has issued a fresh warning to Israel and the United States, with its security chief threatening a severe confrontation if Washington continues it.
articles.body: Iran has issued a fresh warning to Israel and the United States, with its security chief threatening a severe confrontation if Washington continues its blockade and vowing to target US economic interests in the region.Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, said Tehran would "send Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of the Zionist regime, to hell" if tensions escalate again."We will send Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of the Zionist regime, to hell," Rezaei said, according to Iranian state news agency IRIB, in an interview with Al-Manar.Rezaei claimed Netanyahu's actions had brought the "end of the Zionist regime's existence near" and accused the Israeli prime minister of spreading false information about an alleged Iranian plot to assassinate US President Donald Trump's son."Netanyahu has panicked Trump and disrupted his decision-making by spreading false news about an 'Iranian plot to assassinate Trump. Fearing this news, Trump moved around like a food truck worker," he added.Rezaei also warned that any renewed conflict with Israel would enter a new phase, particularly over Lebanon."We are monitoring the situation with full seriousness. Israel will be forced to withdraw from the occupied territories in Lebanon. If the conflict resumes, we are preparing ourselves for a new phase; any future war will be different from the previous ones," Rezaei added.He separately warned Washington against continuing economic pressure on Tehran, saying Iran would retaliate by targeting US economic interests across the region."The US shift to economic pressure demonstrated the futility of military strikes, and we will respond to any escalation of economic tension with countermeasures that target US economic interests in the region," he said."Continuing the siege means a severe confrontation with the American enemy. We exported 80 million barrels of oil during the ceasefire period. If the blockade continues, we will target American economic interests 100 per cent, with intensity and force," Rezaei added.The threats came as Qatar stepped up diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions. articles.title: Former British-Israeli Hamas hostage married in Tel Aviv
articles.summary: Emily Damari, who was held for 15 months, married partner Dani Amit in a ceremony attended by other ex-hostages.
articles.body:
Former British-Israeli hostage Emily Damari has married partner Danielle Amit in a ceremony held in Tel Aviv.

The couple, who met after Damari's release in 2025, have been engaged since January 2026.

Their wedding on Thursday was attended by several of Damari's fellow former hostages, including Romi Gonen, Doron Steinbrecher, Liri Albag, Danielle Gilboa, Omer Shem Tov, Keith and Aviva Siegal, and Gali and Ziv Berma.

Damari, 30, was held in Hamas captivity for more that 15 months after she was kidnapped from her home in southern Israel on 7 October 2023.

She national was shot in the leg and hand in the attack, losing two of her fingers.

In a statement announcing their marriage, the wedding was described as "a joyful new chapter for Emily".

The two brides celebrated with an intimate dinner for family and friends, before exchanging vows beneath the chuppah (traditional Jewish wedding canopy) in bespoke looks by Israeli fashion designer Oria Azran.

Damari's mother Mandy spoke about the 471 days her daughter was held in captivity, and told the couple that their nuptials "means more to me than just a wedding".

"During those endless days and nights, there were moments when the thought of standing here tonight, seeing my daughter alive, safe, happy, and standing beside the person she loves, would have been impossible to imagine," she said.

She went on: "Tonight, I don't want to look back at the 471 days. I want to look forward to all the days ahead".

'After 471 days, Emily is finally home': British-Israeli hostage reunited with mother after release

Damari was taken hostage on 7 October 2023, abducted from a safe room in her home alongside twins Gali and Ziv Berman.

She was one of three hostages released some 15 months later as part of a temporary ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas.

Approximately 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage by Hamas in the 7 October attack.

In response, Israel launched a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,430 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: Tate brothers condemn US jail conditions as they await possible UK extradition
articles.summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate's legal team argued in a Miami court that the two were not a flight risk.
articles.body:
Andrew and Tristan Tate have told a Florida court they should be released from jail so they can fight extradition to the UK on charges of rape and trafficking.

Wearing tan jail uniforms, the brothers maintained they did not commit the alleged crimes as they slammed conditions in US custody.

Government lawyers argued that the two were a flight risk and had bragged about having multiple passports, while defence attorneys said the two social media influencers' high profile would make it almost impossible for them to flee.

US Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis will issue a written ruling at a later date on whether to grant bail to the dual British-US citizens. The two were arrested in Miami on 19 July.

During Thursday's hearing, defence lawyers said the pair had complied with the terms of their release while they battled the UK charges and another case in Romania.

US authorities took the men into custody last month after the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) unveiled dozens of new charges against them.

The British authorities have until 16 September to submit a full extradition request.

Will the Tate brothers be extradited from the US to the UK?

The brothers, who arrived in court in shackles, were questioned in turn by their defence attorneys and government lawyers as they took the stand.

Andrew Tate, 39, declared he has "never committed the crimes I'm accused of".

Tristan Tate, 38, described his detention conditions as small and hot, with little sunlight and exercise.

"It's beginning to grate on me because I can't partake in helping with my defence," he told the court, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

"It's death by scurvy," he said, adding that he had lost 14lb (6.3kg).

The British Embassy filed court documents asking the judge to keep the Tates in custody as the UK pursues extradition.

US government lawyers pushed back against the brothers' claims that they had exaggerated their wealth to massage their online personas.

The federal attorneys said the Tates had access to resources that could help fund an escape and they had bragged about having multiple passports.

But Andrew Tate, a former professional kickboxer, testified that to support himself financially, he "had to go back to the boxing ring against heavier, younger opponents", according to CBS News.

"I've said some stupid things, but sometimes you have to shake the internet to get noticed," he testified about his online statements, according to CBS.

"I'm being treated like El Chapo," he added, referring to the Mexican drug kingpin, "but I have a perfect record in the court system".

Under questioning from his attorney, Joseph McBride, Andrew Tate denied he was a human trafficker.

The defence also called Natasha Sesay, from England, to testify in support of releasing Andrew Tate.

She described a five-year romantic relationship, saying she had had one child with him and was expecting a second.

"It's nice having him at home," she told the court, reports CBS.

Sesay also said that despite his online persona, Andrew Tate "has never ever been violent toward women", according to CBS.

The UK has brought a total of 59 criminal charges against the Tates, including rape and counts relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.

The British authorities filed 21 charges last year against the brothers, then 38 additional counts last month.

The combined charges involve seven accusers, UK prosecutors said.

The brothers also faced sex-trafficking charges in Romania in 2022, and were under a travel ban until they were allowed to come to the US in 2025.

"If I go to England they will lock me up," Tristan Tate said on the stand in Miami on Thursday, "and take everything I've ever worked for".

He also said the Romanian charges had "destroyed my entire life", reports CBS.

"They took everything, even the savings accounts for their [his children's] college funds. This case is make or break for me."

The Tates built an influencer empire in the so-called manosphere, showcasing a lifestyle of conspicuous wealth and excess.

Andrew Tate accumulated millions of followers among an audience of primarily young men.

The White House has said President Donald Trump will not intervene in the extradition case of the brothers, who have been vocal supporters of him.

articles.title: A glacier collapse, flood, now a lake ready to burst: Fresh threat to Nepal
articles.summary: South Asia News: A fresh barrier lake holding around 2 million cubic metres of water has formed on the Nepal side near the confluence of Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsan.
articles.body: A fresh barrier lake holding around 2 million cubic metres of water has formed on the Nepal side near the confluence of Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers close to the Nepal-Tibet border. It was already overflowing Thursday.China’s ministry of water resources warned of a high breach risk over the next three days as another 3 million cubic metres was expected to flow into it. Moderate to heavy rain and thunderstorms forecast through Aug 29 have heightened fears of another surge into Bhote Koshi river a day after Wednesday’s flash flood.For perspective, 2 million cubic metres is enough to cover about 280 standard football pitches — each measuring 105m by 68m, with water one metre deep. The additional 3 million cubic metres expected to flow towards the lake was equivalent to about 420 such pitches.Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo originate in Tibet and merge before crossing into Nepal, where the combined river is known as Bhote Koshi, which then flows into Trishuli river. Any release from the barrier lake could follow the same downstream corridor hit by Wednesday’s flood and threaten settlements farther south as far as the Indian border.Nepal’s national disaster risk reduction and management authority (NDRRMA) issued a warning after receiving information about the blockage from China through the ministry of foreign affairs. “The lake is continuing to grow and there is a risk that it could burst,” NDRRMA said. Flood forecasting division urged people downstream along Bhote Koshi, travellers and rescue workers to stay away from riverbanks.China’s ministry of water resources said it was tracking the lake and running flood simulations to assess the impact of a possible breach. Chinese engineering teams used drones, portable satellite equipment and 3D laser scanners to map the blockage. The footage showed masses of brown water accumulating in a basin with no visible outlet. The weather outlook added to the concern. China’s national meteorological centre forecast rain in Gyirong county through Aug 29, with moderate to heavy spells during some periods. Xinhua quoted chief forecaster Ma Xuekuan as saying afternoon conditions could also bring thunderstorms, strong winds and short spells of intense rainfall.Meanwhile, Basanta Raj Adhikari, director of Centre for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University in Nepal’s capital Kathmandu, warned that “second and third waves” of floods could hit if fresh landslides triggered another surge. “We don’t know yet,” he said, adding that he was in touch with colleagues in China monitoring developments. Adhikari said the episode showed how difficult such Himalayan hazards remained to predict. “Climate change is really happening here,” he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: NOIDA: Raksha Bandhan rush brought traffic across Noida and Ghaziabad to a crawl on Thursday, with commuters facing delays of two to three hours on se.
articles.body: NOIDA: Raksha Bandhan rush brought traffic across Noida and Ghaziabad to a crawl on Thursday, with commuters facing delays of two to three hours on several major roads and expressways. The congestion intensified in the evening, with long queues also reported on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway.Thousands of people working in Gautam Budh Nagar and Ghaziabad were travelling to their hometowns ahead of Raksha Bandhan, putting heavy pressure on roads leading towards western Uttar Pradesh and other districts. Spells of rain further worsened the situation.Commuters complained that despite the festive rush being anticipated, traffic management appeared inadequate and no advisory was issued in Noida to alert motorists about congestion or suggest alternative routes.The worst-affected stretches included the Noida Expressway, sectors 62 and 63, Sector 37, Pari Chowk, Greater Noida-Dadri Road, Vikas Marg, FNG Expressway, Kalindi Kunj, Chilla Border and the DND Flyway.Delhi-bound routes witnessed particularly heavy traffic, with vehicles moving at a sluggish pace around Chilla Border, Kalindi Kunj and the DND Flyway. The queues stretched for several kilometres and waiting times at the border almost doubled.The Noida Expressway also came under pressure as motorists heading towards Greater Noida and beyond tried to avoid congested city roads. Traffic remained slow around Pari Chowk and the Greater Noida-Dadri Road, while FNG Expressway and Vikas Marg also witnessed prolonged snarls.The festive rush was not limited to private vehicles. A large number of passengers headed to bus stops to catch state roadways buses to Agra, Aligarh, Bulandshahr, Ghaziabad, Mathura, Kanpur, Lucknow and other districts. Increased bus movement added to congestion at several locations, while passengers struggled to board buses and move through crowded stretches.In Ghaziabad, long queues were reported on NH-9, around Lal Kuan, Indirapuram, Sector 62 and Dasna. Waterlogging near Mohan Nagar and under the RRTS station further slowed traffic.The traffic department had announced a diversion plan ahead of the festival. Goods vehicles were barred from NH-9 from 8am on August 26 until midnight on August 28. However, traffic pressure mounted as passengers began reaching the highway in large numbers to board buses for their hometowns.ADCP (Traffic) Varun Singh said the restrictions on commercial vehicles had helped to some extent, but the sudden increase in passenger movement led to heavy congestion. More than 900 traffic personnel were deployed to manage the rush, he said.For many commuters, the journey quickly turned into a test of patience.Sanjeev Kumar, who left Noida for Kanpur at 4pm, said he spent an hour just reaching the Sector 62 roundabout on NH-9 and then waited for nearly two hours for a Lucknow-bound bus.“I should have been halfway through my journey by now but it seems that I will spend most of my leave on the commute,” he said.At Lal Kuan, hundreds of passengers waited for buses. Sumit Singh, who was travelling home to Bareilly, said he had already waited for half an hour when a bus arrived, but it was so crowded that passengers were hanging near the doorway.“I decided not to board it,” he said.The situation worsened after sunset, when congestion spread to the Delhi-Meerut Expressway, particularly near its entry and exit points. articles.body:
The death toll in Nepal from devastating flash floods in the border region with China has risen to at least 469, police said on Friday.

Nepalese police said 1,545 people had been rescued, many of them injured.

With three deaths also reported by China, the confirmed toll from the disaster has reached 472. More than 1,400 people are still missing.

Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle told dpa that officials still lacked a clear picture of the number of missing and said it could take several days before the full scale of the disaster was known.

Dozens of bodies have yet to be identified, police said, partly because the force of the floodwaters, mud and debris left many victims badly disfigured or tore bodies apart.

articles.title: Nearly 600 foreign tourists from more than 30 countries are missing in Nepal's flash floods
articles.summary: Among the missing in Nepal are 68 Americans and 25 Canadians, as well as travelers from the UK, Australia, Malaysia, and Ukraine.
articles.body:
Nearly 600 foreign tourists are missing after severe floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border region.

People from over 30 countries, including Americans, Canadians, and Brits, are among those missing.

About 390 bodies have been recovered from the disaster, Nepal police said at 9 p.m. local time on Thursday.

Nearly 600 foreign nationals are missing after deadly floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday.

The flooding began on the morning of August 26, when a surge of water, mud, and debris entered Nepal from the autonomous Chinese region of Tibet via the Bhote Koshi River, Nepal's Tourism Board said.

About 390 bodies have been recovered, per an update by the Nepal police at 9 p.m. local time Thursday. Nepal's foreign ministry said in an update at 8 p.m. that 596 foreign nationals were missing in the country.

The list includes 66 Americans and 25 Canadians, as well as travelers from the UK, Australia, Malaysia, and Ukraine. 167 of the missing foreigners are from neighboring India, authorities said.

In total, people from more than 30 countries are missing.

The US State Department said in a press release that it was deploying a disaster response adviser and providing $500,000 through Catholic Relief Services for shelter, supplies, clean water, and sanitation. It also said the US Embassy in the capital Kathmandu is working with local authorities to locate and assist Americans.

Global Affairs Canada said it was aware that Canadians had been affected and was ready to provide consular assistance. It said power outages were making communications difficult.

The floods hit communities along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers, north of Kathmandu.

The US Geological Survey initially recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake about 40 miles north of the capital. It later updated its event page to say that no earthquake occurred and that the signal came from a glacier collapse and debris flow that released energy equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 earthquake.

What triggered the glacier collapse is still being investigated.

CCTV footage shared online showed walls of water, mud, and debris hitting Gyirong port, the border crossing between the two countries, while other footage showed widespread damage in nearby towns.

Nepal's disaster management authority said 27 foreign tourists had been rescued from Rasuwa by Thursday afternoon. Two army helicopters were deployed to support rescue efforts. The Tourism Board said other parts of Nepal were unaffected. It advised travelers to avoid rivers, bridges, and damaged roads, and to postpone trips to flood-hit areas until officials say conditions are safe.

articles.title: Fresh cash call for Worcester's Angel Place regeneration scheme
articles.summary: The contractor is asking for an extra £1.5m to cover extra costs in order to finish the project.
articles.body:
More public money could be invested in one of Worcestershire's biggest ever regeneration projects as it nears completion.

Malvern-based contractor Speller Metcalfe has requested a final £1.5m contribution towards the completion of the Angel Place regeneration scheme in Worcester.

The project, which includes the refurbishment of the Scala Theatre, requires additional funding to cover a range of extra costs in order to finish it, according to a report to the city council.

The arts centre and wider redevelopment would serve the people of Worcester "for decades to come," said the council leader.

The authority's Policy and Resources Committee will consider the request on 1 September and, if approved, the total cost of the scheme will rise to £26m.

It comes after the city council announced the Scala Theatre would be completed in November, while work on the neighbouring Corn Exchange would be finished in February 2027.

The programme began in 2020 and has been supported by significant grants from the government, as well as investment by the city council.

It has been a long-held ambition of Worcester City Council to revive the historic theatre, which dates back to the 1920s, and was last in use as an amusement arcade.

In 2019, the former cinema appeared in a council "masterplan" for potential redevelopment as part of a wider strategy to inject new life into the northern end of the city centre.

It has not been easy to manage - the original estimated budget in 2020 was just £6.5m, and rose to £12.5m in 2023 before a redesign of the Scala Theatre brought the bill back to just under £10m.

Now councillors are preparing to earmark an extra £1.5m into the project, at a time when budgets are tight.

But the council believes the end result will be transformative with a new arts centre featuring three studio spaces, a bar, a cafe and a regional destination for independent film, live performances and music.

It is also part of a wider overhaul of the Angel Place area, a £26m regeneration which will see the creation of a so-called "northern gateway" into Worcester, an investment which has secured significant financial support from the government.

It includes the relocation of the outdoor market to the Cornmarket - a move which has upset traders - alongside widespread refurbishments of empty buildings and a better-looking public realm.

It is a section of the city which will look and feel radically different from the summer of 2027.

Leader of the council, Lynn Denham, said: "This has been a complex and long-running project and we are pleased it is close to completion now.

"The council is grateful for the sustained partnership commitment from leading local creatives and our construction contractor.

"Scala arts centre will be entertaining and connecting the people of Worcester for decades to come."

articles.title: Manchester Airport warns passengers ahead of busy bank holiday
articles.summary: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday.
articles.body:
Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history.

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk.

It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them.

About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator.

Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage.

"If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said.

Shaw said staff could screen almost 1,000 bags for a large long-haul aircraft and several hundred for a short-haul flight.

"Each bag that fails to pass security checks gets pulled aside, and often needs to be inspected manually," he said.

"This can create delays, but it also creates a risk that your hold bag might not make it onto the plane at all."

The CAA said a fire on board could result in an aircraft being diverted or evacuated.

Vapes, power banks and spare batteries must be carried in the cabin rather than placed in checked baggage.

The CAA advised travellers to check their airline's rules before setting off because additional restrictions may apply.

articles.title: Jersey marine protected areas to expand by further 15%
articles.summary: The government says the marine protected area network is increasing from 6.5% to 21.7% from Tuesday.
articles.body:
The area of sea around Jersey protected against damaging fishing practices is to be expanded by more than 15%.

The government said the marine protected area network, which is territorial waters off limits to trawling and dredging, would be increasing from 6.5% to 21.7%.

It said the measures, coming into force on September 1, would protect some of the island's most important marine habitats, including its sensitive and biodiverse shallow reefs, and would help keep fish stocks sustainable for the fishing industry.

Minister for the Environment Mary Le Hegerat said Jersey's seas were "one of the island's greatest natural assets" and needed continuous protection.

"These measures are evidence-led, have been developed through extensive consultation and form an important part of our long-term vision for the management of Jersey's marine environment," she said.

The government said the protected habitats provided "important structurally complex zones" that acted as nursery and feeding areas for commercially and ecologically important marine life.

It said reducing disturbances in those areas would help build habitat resilience and support healthy marine ecosystems.

Jersey's decision comes as Sark makes a bid to protect 30% of its waters with a proposal submitted to governing body Chief Pleas for approval.

The government said it had delivered the network through the Marine Spatial Plan process with engagement and consultation with Jersey and French fishing representatives, environmental organisations and other marine users since 2023.

It added the impacts of the new measures would be monitored and support would be given to the fishing industry to support it with new fishing areas.

Francis Binney, head of marine resources, said a healthy marine environment and a successful fishing industry "go hand in hand".

He said: "Protecting important habitats today helps ensure Jersey's waters remain productive and biologically rich in the future.

"At the same time, we recognise the challenges facing the fishing industry and are committed to working with fishers to build a resilient and economically sustainable sector."

"This is not about choosing between conservation and fishing - it is about ensuring that Jersey continues to have both healthy seas and a successful fishing industry for decades to come."

articles.title: German troops on NATO’s eastern flank: War has never been this close
articles.summary: How is the German military preparing for a potential conflict on NATO's eastern flank? Euronews spent a week with Germany's Lithuania Brigade and electronic...
articles.body:
Just a few kilometres from the Belarusian border, thousands of NATO troops are focused on one objective: defending Alliance territory in Lithuania. For around six weeks, nearly 3,000 troops – most of them from the German military – trained at Pabradė, using drones, electronic warfare, heavy armour, artillery, infantry, helicopters and fighter jets to practise defending NATO territory against what the military describes as a "conventional aggressor".

A major part of Exercise Freedom Shield I is Germany's 45th Armoured Brigade, also known as the Lithuania Brigade. More than three years ago, Germany decided to permanently station around 4,800 troops in Lithuania by the end of 2027. Spread across two locations, the brigade will comprise five battalions.

But who are the men and women who have chosen to leave Germany and help defend NATO's eastern flank? Euronews accompanied two soldiers from Tank Battalion 203 in Augustdorf, which is due to relocate to Lithuania by the end of 2027.

Corporal Kevin, a driver known as "Rogi", has signed up to serve in the brigade until the end of 2029. Tank commander Staff Sergeant Kevin has volunteered for six years in Lithuania.

Find out why Kevin and Rogi chose to serve in Lithuania in the special Euronews report: "German troops in Lithuania: tanks, drones and deterrence".

German Combat Brigade: 4.800 troops to protect Lithuania

A plaque on Vilnius City Hall – currently hidden behind construction sheeting – carries a quote from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: "Lithuania's security is also our security. Protecting Vilnius means protecting Berlin."

Germany has contributed troops to NATO's multinational battlegroup in Lithuania since 2017 as part of the Alliance's enhanced Forward Presence (eFP), established in response to the growing threat from Russia. But the deployment was based on a rotational model, with troops and equipment regularly replaced rather than permanently stationed in the country.

Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Lithuania pushed for a stronger and more permanent NATO presence. In June 2022, then-Chancellor Olaf Scholz pledged that Germany would lead a brigade in the country. "I promised our friends in Lithuania that Germany would lead a robust Bundeswehr brigade, with a presence on the ground in Lithuania and the ability to be reinforced immediately with troops from Germany in the event of a crisis," Scholz told the Bundestag. "That is solidarity between friends and allies in action."

'It is our mission to provide protection for the eastern flank'

Initially, Germany had not planned to permanently station a fully manned brigade in Lithuania. Only the brigade headquarters was to be based in the country, while combat troops would continue to deploy from Germany for exercises or in the event of a crisis, broadly following the existing rotational model.

According to the German Armed Forces Association , that approach changed in the summer of 2023. The shift came after Wagner chief Yevgeny Prigozhin's failed rebellion against Russia's military leadership and the subsequent relocation of large numbers of Wagner fighters to neighbouring Belarus. The German government said the Wagner mutiny and the movement of mercenaries to Belarus were not the sole reasons for the decision to establish a permanent presence. Berlin acknowledged , however, that the developments had added "further momentum" to the debate.

Germany ultimately changed course. During a visit to troops in Lithuania, Defence Minister Boris Pistorius and Germany's Chief of Defence, General Carsten Breuer, announced that, for the first time in the Bundeswehr's history, a combat-ready brigade would be permanently stationed outside Germany. Pistorius reiterated the commitment in the autumn of 2023: "It is our mission to play a key role in defending NATO's eastern flank."

The plan is to staff the brigade with volunteers. But there are already signs that relying on volunteers alone may not be enough.

'I want soldiers by my side who believe in the mission'

According to the battalion's commander, Lieutenant Colonel Oliver Kaufmann, Tank Battalion 203 has "a very high proportion of volunteers". Speaking to Euronews, Kaufmann said the figures currently being reported needed to be put into context.

"I can speak for my battalion, and the vast majority of soldiers are prepared to go to Lithuania voluntarily. And that is exactly what I want: I want soldiers by my side who believe in the mission and who are ready to take on this important responsibility together as part of the Tank Battalion 203 team," Kaufmann told Euronews.

According to the Bild newspaper, around 60% of the planned brigade has so far been staffed by volunteers, leaving a shortfall of roughly 2,000 troops. Among the forces already stationed in Lithuania, staffing levels stand at 92 %. These include primarily the multinational battlegroup, which has been deployed there since 2017.

Tank Battalion 203 and Panzergrenadier Battalion 122 are not due to relocate to Lithuania until 2027. According to Bild's reporting, those units are still around 40 % short of the personnel they need.

"They are all volunteers. Of course, there are occasional shortages, particularly among specialists, such as IT and logistics personnel, although it is not limited to those areas. It is no different from what we see back home. We are continuing to rely on volunteers and are offering their families the best possible conditions. Once we have exhausted all the options available to us, we will look at alternatives," the minister said.

Euronews accompanied soldiers who volunteered to go to Lithuania

Pistorius added, however, that being posted elsewhere was "nothing unusual" for Bundeswehr soldiers, should relying on volunteers prove insufficient.

Euronews spent a week with different Bundeswehr units in Lithuania and heard mixed views on the issue. Some agreed with Pistorius, while others said they believed soldiers with families might be less willing to make the move. While soldiers will be able to fly regularly between Vilnius and Germany, "service in Lithuania will not fundamentally differ from normal military life in Germany". That means exercises, guard duty, periods on standby and other military duties may also take place at weekends.

Beyond the political decisions and debates over troop numbers and deterrence are the soldiers who will ultimately carry out the mission.

Euronews followed two members of the brigade to find out why they volunteered to serve in Lithuania, what they expect from their new mission and what a permanent posting will mean for them personally.

Watch the full Euronews report, "German troops in Lithuania: tanks, drones and deterrence", to find out more.
